description: Text for: Fuel for a boom-town depot.

title: Fuel for the depot at {destination}
{tonnes} t of {cargo} for {destination}
Fill the tanks at {destination}
ctx: Traffic at {destination} has outrun the depot's tanks. Ships are queueing to leave empty.
The new depot at {destination} opened with a full house and a half-empty tank.
A trade boom is burning more fuel than the outer systems can make. The depot at {destination} is first to run dry.
{destination} is a stop between two lanes and a hundred ships want its fuel. It has some.
task: Haul {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} within {deadline}.
Bring {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination}. It must arrive sealed and not rattled.
Take the {cargo} to {destination} in {deadline}. Ships are waiting on the dock.
Deliver {tonnes} t of {cargo} to the depot at {destination} within {deadline}.
success: The tanks fill and the queue clears. {faction} pays {reward}.
The depot opens its pumps within the hour. {faction} pays {reward}.
The first ship fuels from your delivery before you've finished the paperwork. {faction} pays {reward}.
Pumps running. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The depot ran dry while you were en route. {faction} pays nothing.
The fuel arrived late and the queue had left. {faction} withholds the fee.
The cargo did not arrive. {faction} will remember it when the next boom starts.

description: Text for: Survey an empty system.

title: Survey #empty# {destination}
#chart.cap# {destination}, #bare#
Fresh charts of {destination}
ctx: Nobody has filed a survey of {destination}. The old charts show a star and a guess.
{destination} is a blank on every map we hold, and a blank is worth nothing to anyone who wants to file a claim.
The gate points at {destination} and nobody has ever gone through with an instrument case.
Somebody will claim {destination} before long. Whoever holds the survey holds the first word.
task: Fly a full survey: star class, planets, belts, gate approaches. Scan each body once and log it.
Make a pass of every body you can reach, scan it and bring the log back.
Scan the star, each world and the belts, and note anything that looks hazardous or worth digging.
Fly the system end to end, scanning as you go. Close passes where the sensors ask for them.
success: The log is complete and the chart room goes quiet while it reads it. {faction} pays {reward}.
{faction} loads your survey into its registers before you've left the dock. {reward} is credited.
The system now has a name on a chart and your ship's mark beside it. {faction} pays {reward}.
Clean data, no gaps. {faction} pays {reward} and asks if you are free next week.
failure: The survey is patchy and the gaps are where the money would have been. {faction} withholds payment.
Without a full log {faction} has to send someone else. They will not forget who left holes in the chart.
The deadline passes and a rival's survey is filed first. {faction} has no use for yours.

description: Text for: Prospect a strike for the rush.

title: Prospect the strike at {destination}
Rush survey: {destination}
Is {destination} worth the fuss?
ctx: Word of a rich strike at {destination} has reached every bar from here to the next gate, and half of it is made up.
Prospectors are queuing for {destination}. Somebody should check what they are queuing for.
There is ore at {destination}, or there is a rumour of ore. A rumour is a poor basis for a mine.
The rush is on and claim stakes are going into rock at {destination} faster than anyone can value them.
task: Scan the seams, drill a few test cores and bring back honest numbers on grade and tonnage.
Take core samples from the main belt, rate the grade and send the figures back before the crowd does.
Run a density scan across the field and log the five richest bodies. Do not mark any of them as yours.
Test the strike. If it is real, say how big. If it is salted rock, say that instead.
success: Your numbers are better than the rumours, and for once somebody is pleased about it. {faction} pays {reward}.
The strike is real and now {faction} has the figures first. It pays {reward}.
You saved {faction} a very expensive mistake with a very cheap survey. {reward} is yours.
The cores check out. {faction} pays {reward} and starts hiring.
failure: The numbers came back too late to matter. The crowd had already staked the best of it. {faction} pays nothing.
Your report was vague about grade. {faction} will not bet a mine on vague.
{faction} wanted the figures first and got them third. The fee is withheld.

description: Text for: Scan a gas giant.

title: Skim the giant at {destination}
Gas giant scan: {destination}
Deep atmosphere profile, {destination}
ctx: The giant at {destination} has never been profiled below the cloud tops. Our fuel estimates are guesses and our guesses are expensive.
A skimming depot is only worth building if the atmosphere holds what the models say it does, and at {destination} nobody has looked.
{destination} has a giant with banded storms and a magnetic field that the old charts disagree about.
The light is poor and the winds are worse at {destination}, which is why the data is so thin.
task: Drop to the upper cloud layers on a scanning run, log the composition and climb out before the shear takes your hull.
Make three passes through the upper atmosphere and take your scans at the marked depths.
Sample the gas at each marked altitude, plot the storm edges and log the hydrogen fraction.
Fly the skimmer line, scan the field strength at the poles and bring everything home in one piece.
success: The profile is better than the model, which has been quietly deleted. {faction} pays {reward}.
You came out of the clouds with a full log and a hull that needs washing. {faction} pays {reward}.
Every depth is covered. {faction} credits {reward} and reaches for the planning tables.
The storm edges are exactly where you said they were. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The scan stopped halfway down. {faction} has a half profile and half a plan.
The data is too noisy to use, and {faction} cannot build a depot on noise. No payment.
You turned back early. Probably sensible, but {faction} is not paying for sensible.

description: Text for: Chart a gate approach.

title: Chart the approach to {destination}
Gate approach survey: {destination}
Safe lanes into {destination}
ctx: Traffic is rising and the lane into {destination} is still marked by a few rocks and someone's memory.
The gate at {destination} is a long way from the nearest light, and ships arriving there have to guess where the debris is.
A trade boom is pushing hulls through {destination} faster than the charts can keep up with.
Every captain who comes through {destination} drifts a little off line, and the drift has already cost one hull.
task: Fly the approach at three speeds, log every hazard and mark a clean lane.
Map the debris, the shadow zones and any rock that moves. Publish a lane we can put on the public chart.
Scan the corridor from the gate to the first safe holding point and mark the traffic bends.
Tag each hazard with a position and a drift rate. We will build the lane around your numbers.
success: The lane goes on the public chart with your tag in the margin. {faction} pays {reward}.
Two freighters use your corridor before you've finished docking. {faction} pays {reward}.
Every hazard is logged and one of them is a surprise. {faction} pays {reward} and quietly thanks you.
The approach is safer by evening. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The lane has gaps, and a hauler found one of them. {faction} blames the survey and will not pay.
The deadline passes with the approach half charted. {faction} pays nothing for half a lane.
Your log lists the hazards but not where they are. {faction} sends it back.

description: Text for: Plant survey beacons.

title: Plant {tonnes} t of beacons at {destination}
Beacon line to {destination}
Mark {destination} for the map
ctx: A system with no beacons is a system nobody will fly to. {destination} has none.
We hold the right to mark {destination}, and we have the hardware. What we lack is someone to put it in the right places.
The {cargo} in your hold is a string of nav beacons. They only work when they sit at the points we have marked.
Our survey of {destination} is done. The marking is not, and ships are already asking for it.
task: Take {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} and plant each unit at its marked point. Check that each one answers the ping.
Carry the {cargo} out, drop the beacons on the listed coordinates and bring back the confirmation log.
Set the beacons along the marked line, test each against the next, and leave none unlit.
success: The line lights up one beacon at a time. {faction} pays {reward}.
Every beacon answers. {faction} pays {reward} and starts writing the sailing notes.
The last unit blinks on and the system has a shape. {faction} pays {reward}.
The marked line holds. {faction} credits {reward}.
failure: Three beacons are dark and one is in the wrong place. {faction} withholds payment.
The beacons never made it to the marks. {faction} writes the {cargo} off and does not forget it.
With the deadline gone, the line is useless to the ships already arriving. No payment.

description: Text for: Survey a system that does not add up.

title: A strange count at {destination}
Check the survey of {destination}
{destination} does not add up
odd: The planets are in the right place and the right number, and the orbital timing is wrong by a margin that does not reduce.
Our probe counted one more moon than the last probe, and neither count has an error bar.
The mass of the system is not the sum of its parts. We have checked the parts.
One of the survey drones returned an image of a world with a coastline. The next pass showed no world.
The star is a sensible star. Its light curve is not, and we have no model that fits.
Three independent scans of the same belt disagree, and the disagreement has a pattern.
ctx: We have a survey of {destination} that does not add up. #odd#
{destination} is giving us numbers we cannot reconcile. #odd#
A drone came back from {destination} with a log that is internally consistent and externally absurd. #odd#
task: Fly the system, run the scans again and report what you find. Do not offer an explanation. We want the readings.
Repeat the survey and log every discrepancy. Raw data only. Do not tidy it.
Survey the marked bodies. If the numbers do not agree with ours, send both sets and leave the arguing to us.
Go and measure it properly. Report only what the instruments say, even if the instruments contradict each other.
coda: Whatever it was, it does not appear on the second pass.
The numbers agree with each other and with nothing else. Nobody has an explanation.
The old men in the chart room read it twice and put it in a drawer.
The readings are filed. The question stays open.
success: The data is clean and the contradictions are intact. #coda# {faction} pays {reward}.
Your log matches the drone's, and neither matches the charts. #coda# {faction} pays {reward}.
You found exactly what the first team found, which is the unsettling part. {faction} pays {reward}. #coda#
{faction} reads your readings in silence and pays {reward}. #coda#
failure: The instruments gave you nothing usable. {faction} cannot tell whether that is the system or the sensors, and will not pay to find out.
You came back with a tidy explanation and no data. {faction} has no use for explanations.
The survey was cut short. {faction} will send someone braver, or someone with a better hull.

description: Text for: Map ruins for a light elf house.

title: Mapping for the house at {destination}
The ruins of {destination}
A quiet survey, {destination}
ctx: The house holds an old interest in {destination}. It prefers not to say why.
There are ruins at {destination} of a kind the house considers its own concern. We would like them recorded accurately and discreetly.
The house wants an exact survey of the ruins at {destination}. It has seen an unreliable one already.
The ruins at {destination} have been stirring, or the sensors say they have. The house wants a record before someone else makes one.
task: Map the structures: positions, dimensions and any marked surfaces. Take no samples and move nothing.
Chart every structure and note any that are powered. Touch nothing, and leave nothing behind.
Record the layout as precisely as your instruments allow. You will find nothing to remove. Remove nothing.
Survey the site in full and send the log to the house alone. Copies are not wanted.
success: The house receives the log with perfect courtesy and says little. {faction} pays {reward}.
Your map is accepted. Nobody explains what it will be used for, and {faction} pays {reward}.
The steward reads the survey, then reads one page again, and closes the folder. {faction} pays {reward}.
Every structure is recorded. {faction} pays {reward}, and the matter does not come up again.
failure: The site is not mapped and the house is displeased, and displeasure from the house is long. {faction} pays nothing.
Parts of the survey are missing. The house does not ask why. It simply declines payment.
Your log was seen by someone else first. {faction} withdraws the commission and a good deal of goodwill.

description: Text for: Dig-site mapping for a survey society.

title: Dig-site survey at {destination}
Map the ruin field, {destination}
Elder structures at {destination}
ctx: We have a dig site at {destination} and half a plan of it. The other half is under rubble.
A field of elder ruins sits on the far side of {destination}, and the three previous surveys each put them somewhere different.
The ruins at {destination} are older than the gate, if the stonework is to be believed. We would like them on paper.
Our team went out to {destination} and returned with a mapping gap and several theories. The gap is the useful part.
task: Fly a low grid over the site, scan every structure and mark its position against the gate beacon.
Scan the field in a grid, mark entrances, and log any surface carvings you can resolve.
Map the surface and the first level of any open shafts. Send images of anything that looks like writing.
Plot the ruin field and flag anything that moved between your first pass and your last.
success: The grid is complete and the structures line up. The society is quietly delighted. {faction} pays {reward}.
Your survey gives the members something new to argue about. {faction} pays {reward}.
The carvings resolve cleanly. Nobody can read them, but they can be copied. {faction} pays {reward}.
The field is on paper at last. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The grid has holes where the ruins are densest. {faction} cannot publish a map with holes.
Too little of the site was recorded. {faction} withholds the fee and tells the other captains why.
The imaging failed halfway. The ruins are exactly as unmapped as before.

description: Text for: Survey where ships go quiet.

title: Quiet space at {destination}
Radio check at {destination}
Why {destination} is quiet
ctx: Two survey drones went into {destination} and stopped reporting at nearly the same moment. Neither was damaged by anything we can name.
Ships have stopped talking inside {destination}. Their beacons keep running. Their voices do not.
We lost a probe at {destination}, then found a second probe's log that says it was in two places for an hour.
The traffic through {destination} has not stopped. The chatter has.
task: Fly in with your own recorder running and log every channel. Come out and bring the file.
Survey the system on passive sensors only and note where the quiet starts.
Map the silence. Log every point where your comms drop and every point where they return.
Run the standard survey and add a signal sweep at each stop. We want to know whether anything is out there.
coda: There was nothing in the log that anyone could name.
The silence began and ended at points that no object marks.
The recorder is clean. The silence in it is very clean.
Nobody has a theory and everybody has an opinion.
success: You came back, which is more than the drones did. #coda# {faction} pays {reward}.
The recording is thirty minutes of nothing and the society treats it as treasure. {faction} pays {reward}. #coda#
The log shows your comms dropping and returning on schedule. #coda# {faction} pays {reward}.
{faction} listens to the quiet twice and pays {reward}. #coda#
failure: No recording, no payment. {faction} has lost three drones and a captain to this system and is unlikely to try a fourth.
You turned back before the quiet began. {faction} understands, and pays nothing.
The file is corrupt. {faction} says the corruption is interesting and withholds the fee anyway.

description: Text for: Escort a claim ship.

title: Escort the claim ship to {destination}
Claim run: {destination}
Cover for the claimants at {destination}
ctx: Our claim ship is carrying the writ for {destination}, the stakes and a crew that has never seen a pirate. A rival wants the writ.
The claim at {destination} is good in law and thin in practice. The first ship to plant a marker wins, and ours is slow.
We have the right to {destination}. A second party has the speed. We need someone with guns to make up the difference.
The claim ship is full of surveyors and stakes, and it moves like a barn.
task: Fly escort to {destination}, stay in formation and make sure the claim ship plants its marker before anyone else does.
See the claim ship through to {destination}. Stay close, shoot anyone who closes faster than you like.
Keep the claim ship alive until it has set the marker at {destination}.
Cover the claim ship on the whole run to {destination} and stay until the marker lights.
success: The marker lights and the claim is lodged. {faction} pays {reward}.
The claim ship docks with all its stakes. {faction} pays {reward} and starts setting out the first camp.
The stakes go in the ground and the rival turns away. {faction} pays {reward}.
The claim holds. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The claim ship was lost and the writ with it. {faction} has a lot to say and none of it is {reward}.
A rival planted first. {faction} pays nothing for a second place.
The claim ship arrived late and empty-handed. {faction} withholds the fee.

description: Text for: Escort a breakaway claim.

title: A free claim at {destination}
Escort the settlers to {destination}
Flag and stakes for {destination}
ctx: The people of {destination} want out of the charter the core has had them under. Their first act is a new claim, filed under their own seal.
The settlement at {destination} is declaring itself, and the surveyors are going out ahead of the flag.
A claim at {destination} under an independent seal will annoy several governments. We would like it done before they have finished being annoyed.
The old charter says nothing about {destination}. The new one says a great deal.
task: Escort our claim ship to {destination} and keep it clear of any patrol, tax boat or ambitious neighbour.
Fly cover until the claim ship has planted the new marker at {destination}.
See the settlers' ship through to {destination} without it being boarded.
Escort the claim vessel, hold off interference and stay until the marker is up.
success: The new marker blinks and a small crowd cheers. {faction} pays {reward}.
The claim is planted and the customs boat arrives an hour late. {faction} pays {reward}.
The settlers raise their flag over a patch of rock. {faction} pays {reward}.
It is filed. Several governments will object and none of them will do much. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The claim ship was boarded short of {destination}. {faction} does not pay, and does not forgive.
The marker never went up. {faction} says the cause will need another escort and another captain.
A patrol turned the settlers back. {faction} pays nothing.

description: Text for: Escort a survey ship.

title: Escort a survey ship to {destination}
Guard the survey boat, {destination}
Fly cover for the cartographers
ctx: The survey ship bound for {destination} carries no guns and several people who have never been shot at.
{destination} lies beyond the last patrolled gate. The survey team goes out in a converted tug.
We have a team that wants to survey {destination} and a hull that cannot survive a second look from a raider.
Surveyors collect data. They do not, as a rule, collect enemies. They have collected one anyway.
task: Escort the survey ship to {destination} and stay with it through its first pass.
Fly alongside until the survey ship has completed its scan and is ready to return.
Keep the survey ship clear of trouble to {destination} and back.
Cover the survey ship for the whole survey. Break contact only when the data is aboard.
success: The survey ship docks with its data intact and its crew speechless. {faction} pays {reward}.
The tug and its scientists are home. {faction} pays {reward} and offers you a place on the next expedition.
Everyone is accounted for. {faction} pays {reward}.
Not a scratch on the survey boat. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The survey ship took a hit and turned back. {faction} pays nothing and has a repair bill.
You lost the survey ship. {faction} has a memorial to arrange and no further commission for you.
The ship made it. Its data did not. {faction} withholds the fee.

description: Text for: Escort hold prospectors.

title: Hold prospectors to {destination}
Escort the drill barge, {destination}
A dwarf crew for {destination}
ctx: The hold has sent a prospecting barge to {destination}. It is slow, heavy and carries a good deal of equipment, which attracts interest.
There is a field at {destination} that the hold intends to dig. The barge is mostly drills and bad-tempered dwarves.
Our drill barge sets out for {destination} on a schedule that lets any raider with a clock know where it will be.
We have a barge, a crew and a contract. We want a hull with guns that will take the risk off the first two.
task: Escort the barge to {destination} and stay until its drills are down.
Fly cover for the barge the whole way and see it into the field safely.
Keep raiders and rivals off the barge to {destination}. It is slow. Plan for slow.
Escort the barge from the gate to the field and stay until the first cores are lifted.
success: The barge sets its drills and the first core comes up clean. {faction} pays {reward}.
The hold's crew send down the first sample and begin to complain about the sample. {faction} pays {reward}.
The barge arrived whole. {faction} pays {reward}, to the credit.
The drills are down. {faction} pays {reward} and not a credit more.
failure: The barge is damaged and the crew are furious. {faction} cites the contract and pays nothing.
The barge did not reach the field. {faction} notes the clause and withholds the fee.
You left the barge before the drills were down. The contract does not allow for that.

description: Text for: Deliver a colony's first habitat.

title: First habitat for {destination}
{tonnes} t of prefab for {destination}
A roof for {destination}
ctx: The colony at {destination} has an air supply, a charter and a tent. It needs a habitat.
Settlers are already at {destination}, sleeping in their ship. The first habitat unit will let them leave it.
{destination} gets its first permanent building when you arrive, assuming you do.
The colony at {destination} is two weeks from the first cold snap and has no walls.
task: Haul {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} within {deadline}. Keep it sealed and do not bend the frames.
Carry {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination}. The frame sections are delicate and the colonists cannot replace them.
Take the {cargo} to {destination} and keep it dry, level and unscratched. Deadline {deadline}.
Deliver {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} in {deadline}. It is everything the colony has.
success: The sections are bolted together before the sun is down. {faction} pays {reward}.
The first wall goes up and the colonists cheer a wall. {faction} pays {reward}.
They move in the same night. {faction} pays {reward}.
The habitat stands. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The sections did not arrive. The colony sleeps in its ship for another month. {faction} pays nothing.
{faction} reports the frames bent in transit and refuses payment.
The cold came first. {faction} has a long list of complaints and no {reward}.

description: Text for: First supply run to a new colony.

title: First supply run to {destination}
Supplies for the new colony at {destination}
{tonnes} t of {cargo} for {destination}
ctx: The colony at {destination} has been alive for a few weeks. It is short of nearly everything and long on optimism.
{destination} is a settlement of tents and a prefab habitat, still waiting on its first resupply.
{destination} needs more than it has, and has not yet worked out how much more.
The settlers at {destination} wrote a list. It is a short list. They will add to it.
task: Haul {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} within {deadline}.
Bring {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination}. Check it twice before you leave.
Deliver {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} in {deadline}. The colony is counting the days.
Take the {cargo} out to {destination}. {tonnes} t, sealed, before {deadline} are up.
success: The settlers carry it off the ramp by hand, grateful. {faction} pays {reward}.
The first supply run lands. The colony sets about being a colony. {faction} pays {reward}.
They've unpacked the {cargo} before you leave. {faction} pays {reward} and the settlers press a small gift on you.
The shelves of the colony store look less bare. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The supplies arrived after the colonists had given up and gone. {faction} pays nothing.
The {cargo} never turned up. {faction} sends an apology to the colony and an invoice to you.
The colony ran short while you were late. {faction} remembers.

description: Text for: Mining gear for a new outpost.

title: Drill heads for {destination}
{tonnes} t of mining gear, {destination}
Outfit the outpost at {destination}
ctx: The outpost at {destination} has staked its claim and has nothing to cut rock with.
Our new outpost at {destination} has a crew, a pad and no equipment. The rush is making sure everyone else has sold out.
The seams at {destination} will not dig themselves, and the last of our own stock is on someone else's ship.
The rush has pushed prices for drill heads up and availability down. We found some. They are not at {destination}.
task: Haul {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} within {deadline}.
Bring {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination}. Handle it as if you were paying for it.
Take the {cargo} to {destination} in {deadline}. The outpost's crew is idle and wages run.
Deliver {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination}. Do not stop for anyone who offers to buy it.
success: The heads are in the rigs by nightfall. {faction} pays {reward}.
The outpost is digging before you have undocked. {faction} pays {reward}.
The crew fits the first head before the manifest is signed. {faction} pays {reward}.
Everything arrived in working order. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The gear arrived late and the crew is already gone. {faction} pays nothing.
{faction} says the heads were damaged. It does not offer to pay for the damage or the delivery.
The outpost had to buy at rush prices while you were late. {faction} will not pay for that.

description: Text for: Supplies for a breakaway settlement.

title: Supplies to the free settlement at {destination}
{tonnes} t of {cargo}, no questions
Relief for {destination}
ctx: {destination} has declared for itself and the old suppliers have declared against it.
The settlers at {destination} left their charter and the charter's shops went with it.
Supply convoys now steer clear of {destination}, which is a polite way of imposing a blockade.
We cannot pay the old suppliers' prices and they will not take our new currency.
task: Haul {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} within {deadline}. Expect a customs boat and answer it politely.
Bring {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination}. There will be a patrol. We would prefer it did not find you.
Take the {cargo} to {destination}. Declare it honestly. The cargo is legal, which is the whole point.
Deliver {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} in {deadline}. The old authority will object to it, and has no grounds.
success: The shelves fill. The settlement hangs out a flag in your honour. {faction} pays {reward}.
The shipment is unloaded to quiet applause. {faction} pays {reward}.
They ring the settlement bell when you dock. {faction} pays {reward}.
The first delivery to the free settlement lands. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: A patrol turned you back. {faction} pays nothing and has made a note of your name.
The supplies were seized. {faction} blames you and does not offer a second chance.
The settlement ran short. {faction} withholds the fee and tells the other captains why.

description: Text for: Prospect an asteroid field.

title: Prospect the field at {destination}
Asteroid survey: {destination}
What is in the rocks at {destination}?
ctx: There is a field at {destination} that has never been drilled. Nobody knows what is in it, and finding out costs less than guessing.
{destination} has an asteroid belt on every chart and an assay on none of them.
The belt at {destination} looks promising from far away. It has looked promising from far away for years.
A claim on {destination} is worth the grade of its rock, and no one has measured the grade.
task: Fly the field, scan and sample the bigger rocks, and report the five most promising.
Take core samples from a dozen bodies and bring back the assay.
Run a density sweep, drill a few test holes and plot the grades.
Prospect the belt and report back with grade, tonnage and the best place to start.
success: The assay is solid and the best rocks are marked. {faction} pays {reward}.
Some of the belt is worthless and some of it is excellent, and you can tell which. {faction} pays {reward}.
Your samples come back richer than hoped. {faction} pays {reward}.
The assay is filed and a claim is already being drawn up. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The samples were contaminated and the assay is useless. {faction} pays nothing.
You surveyed the wrong rocks. {faction} has no use for the right answer to the wrong question.
Too few cores, too many guesses. {faction} withholds the fee.

description: Text for: Mine a quota for a hold.

title: Mine {tonnes} t of {cargo}
Quota: {tonnes} t of {cargo} for {destination}
Fill the hold with {cargo}
ctx: The rush has drained the stockpile at {destination}. The smelters there will not run without ore.
The seams at {system} are open and the quota at {destination} is not filled.
Our own crews are too few for a quota this size. The rush has doubled the work and not the workforce.
